title: Adding a New Transformation Step
text: Use template starting point:
code: #' Run {Step Name} Step #' #' {Brief description of what this step does and its purpose}. #' Implements the '{stepname}' transformation step from the Model #' Parameters pipeline. #' #' @param mod Model object #' @param file Path to {stepname} step specification file #' @return Updated model object with {description of added data} #' @keywords internal .run_step_{stepname} <- function(mod, file) {   # Load the step specification file   mod <- .add_file(mod, file)   step_data <- .get_file(mod, file)    # Verify required columns exist in the specification file   .verify_columns(     step_data,     c("column1", "column2", "column3"),     "{stepname} step file",     file   )    # Process each row in the step specification   for (i in seq_len(nrow(step_data))) {     info <- step_data[i, ]      # Extract parameters from the specification     param1 <- info[["column1"]]     param2 <- info[["column2"]]     param3 <- info[["column3"]]      # Implement your transformation logic here     # Example: mod$data[new_column] <- transformation(mod$data[existing_column])   }    # Return the updated model object   mod }

title: Adding a New Transformation Step

Verify Columns: Validates specification file contains required columns. Update column list match step’s requirements Model Parameters documentation. Process Row: loop processes row specification file. row typically defines one transformation apply. Access Data: Read data: mod$data[column_name] mod$data[[column_name]] Write data: mod$data[new_column] <- transformed_values Return Updated Model: Always return mod end transformations can chained.
code: mod <- .add_file(mod, file) step_data <- .get_file(mod, file) .verify_columns(step_data,                 c("column1", "column2", "column3"),                 "{stepname} step file",                 file)

title: Adding a New Transformation Step
text: ’s real example existing codebase (R/step-center.R): function: - defined source file R/step-center.R - Loads center specification file - Verifies required columns (origVariable, centerValue, centeredVariable) - row, creates new centered variable subtracting centerValue original variable - Returns updated model new columns added mod$data
code: .run_step_center <- function(mod, file) {   mod <- .add_file(mod, file)   step_data <- .get_file(mod, file)   .verify_columns(     step_data,     c("origVariable", "centerValue", "centeredVariable"),     "center step file",     file   )    for (i in seq_len(nrow(step_data))) {     info <- step_data[i, ]     orig_variable <- info[["origVariable"]]     center_value <- info[["centerValue"]]     centered_variable <- info[["centeredVariable"]]      mod$data[centered_variable] <- mod$data[orig_variable] - center_value   }    mod }

what: What is the Model Parameters Specification?
title: Introduction to Model Parameters Pipeline
text: Model Parameters specification standardized way define apply data transformations used predictive algorithms. developed Big Life Lab predictive health models : HTNPoRT: Hypertension Population Risk Tool DemPoRT: Dementia Population Risk Tool CVDPoRT: Cardiovascular Disease Population Risk Tool MPoRT: Mortality Population Risk Tool specification uses CSV files define transformations, making algorithms: Transparent: parameters transformations documented human-readable files Portable: model can deployed across different platforms programming languages Reproducible: Transformations applied consistently

title: Introduction to Model Parameters Pipeline
text: pipeline supports five types transformations: Center: Subtracts constant value variables (e.g., age - 50) Dummy: Creates binary indicator variables categorical values Interaction: Multiplies variables together create interaction terms RCS: Applies restricted cubic spline transformations non-linear relationships Logistic Regression: Applies logistic regression generate predictions

title: Introduction to Model Parameters Pipeline
text: HTNPoRT (Hypertension Population Risk Tool) validated predictive model hypertension risk. ’s use package HTNPoRT:
code: # Clone the HTNPoRT repository to get model parameters and validation data # In your terminal: # git clone https://github.com/Big-Life-Lab/htnport.git  library(model.parameters.pipeline)  # Set path to cloned HTNPoRT repository htnport_dir <- "/path/to/htnport"  # Load validation data data_file <- file.path(   htnport_dir,   "output/validation-data/HTNPoRT-female-validation-data.csv" ) data <- read.csv(data_file)  # View the input data structure head(data)  # Path to model export file model_export_file <- file.path(   htnport_dir,   "output/logistic-model-export/female/HTNPoRT-female-model-export.csv" )  # Prepare the model pipeline mod <- prepare_model_pipeline(model_export_file)  # Run the pipeline mod <- run_model_pipeline(mod, data = data)  # View the transformed data with all intermediate steps head(mod$data)  # Extract logistic predictions (hypertension risk probabilities) predictions <- mod$data[, grep("^logistic_", names(mod$data))] head(predictions)  # Summary statistics of predictions summary(predictions)
